The specification schema

Source: vignettes/tte-spec-schema.Rmd
tte-spec-schema.Rmd

Why the schema exists

tteplan_read_spec() refuses every key the schema does not name. Without the gate, swereg would ignore a key it does not read, and say nothing.

For example, a cohort restriction under inclusion_criteria$additional_inclusion would never reach the eligibility filter, because swereg does not read that key path. The study population would stay unrestricted, and no message would say so. The specification would look exactly like one that works.

One table names every legal key path. It is .TTE_SPEC_SCHEMA, in R/tteplan_spec_schema.R, and nothing else in swereg holds that list. Every table below is generated from that object, so the tables and the gate use the same list.

How a key path is written

A path is written the way the walker over the parsed YAML produces it.

  • The root is $.
  • A mapping key appends /<key>.
  • A sequence index becomes [].

A treatment block therefore has the path $/enrollments[]/treatment. Every element of a sequence shares one path, so the schema states one rule for all of them.

The path is what separates two keys that share a name. $/enrollments[]/additional_inclusion is accepted. $/inclusion_criteria/additional_inclusion is refused. A table keyed by the key name alone cannot state that.

Each context declares its own children. There is no generic rule for an implementation block. A treatment implementation, an outcome implementation and a confounder implementation accept different keys.

The two key classes

Each key path carries one class.

schema <- swereg:::.TTE_SPEC_SCHEMA

rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(schema), function(context) {
  node <- schema[[context]]
  keys <- list(
    consumed = node[["consumed"]],
    metadata = node[["metadata"]]
  )
  data.frame(
    context = context,
    key = unlist(keys, use.names = FALSE),
    class = rep(names(keys), lengths(keys)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))
rows <- rows[order(rows$context, rows$key), ]

# Wrap a path in backticks. A bare `$` opens inline maths in a pipe table, and
# pandoc then merges the cells it spans.
as_code <- function(x) paste0("`", x, "`")

knitr::kable(
  as.data.frame(table(rows$class), stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
  col.names = c("class", "key paths")
)
class key paths
consumed 130
metadata 10
class what swereg does with the key a specification that carries it
consumed swereg reads it. accepted
metadata swereg accepts it and never reads it. accepted

Every other key is refused. A retired key is refused the same way: swereg keeps no list of old key names.

Why one class is not enough

A one-class table holds “swereg reads it”, and refuses everything else. Under that table, every key swereg does not read is refused. That table would refuse the valid key paths below.

meta <- rows[rows$class == "metadata", ]
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(context = as_code(meta$context), key = as_code(meta$key)),
  row.names = FALSE
)
context key
$/open_questions[] resolution
$/standing_methods admin_censoring
$/standing_methods comparator_to_intervention_ratio_default
$/standing_methods matching_ratio_default
$/standing_methods/admin_censoring handling
$/standing_methods/admin_censoring note
$/standing_methods/comparator_to_intervention_ratio_default handling
$/standing_methods/comparator_to_intervention_ratio_default note
$/standing_methods/matching_ratio_default handling
$/standing_methods/matching_ratio_default note

Each one records a decision for a human reader. $/open_questions[]/resolution records how the study team settled an open question. $/standing_methods/admin_censoring records the administrative censoring rule. R/ names both only in the schema, and reads neither value. The metadata class lets the gate refuse an unknown key and accept these.

The design keys

Every specification MUST declare two flat top-level keys. They are design choices, so the specification holds them and no function argument does.

period_width: 4
admin_censoring_isoyearweek: "2025-01"
Key Meaning Type Required
period_width The width in weeks of the enrollment period. The same width sets each follow-up interval. One whole number of at least 1 Yes
admin_censoring_isoyearweek The administrative censoring week. Follow-up includes that week. One string YYYY-WW, with the week from 01 to 53 Yes

tteplan_read_spec() stops on a specification without one or both keys, and on a bad value. The one message names both keys, states each problem and shows the example above. tteplan_check_spec() reports the same message as one read_error row on the path $. s0 reads both values from the specification. It does not compare the week with the skeleton.

$/standing_methods/admin_censoring stays an optional metadata note. swereg does not read it. When the note states a week, keep it equal to admin_censoring_isoyearweek.

The global inclusion container

inclusion_criteria is a fixed container. It holds isoyears and criteria, and nothing else.

inclusion_criteria:
  isoyears: [2010, 2023]
  criteria:
    - name: "Recorded gender dysphoria diagnosis"
      rationale: "The study population is people with the diagnosis"
      type: has_event
      implementation:
        source_variable: osd_f64
        window: lifetime_before_baseline

Each entry declares one type, and inclusion_criteria$criteria accepts three. It declares type: has_event as its own key, one level above implementation:. It declares a washout under implementation: instead, as type: no_prior_value or type: only_prior_value. tteplan_read_spec() refuses any other type, and it refuses an entry that declares both an outer type and an inner one. A criterion swereg reads and ignores never restricts the study population, and it looks exactly like one that does.

tteplan_apply_exclusions() adds one eligibility column for each criterion, and the criterion’s type sets the column name.

  • has_event gives eligible_has_<variable>_<window>.
  • no_prior_value gives eligible_no_<variable>_<window>.
  • only_prior_value gives eligible_only_<variable>_<window>.

tteplan_apply_exclusions() then combines every eligibility column into eligible.

How it differs from a per-enrollment additional_inclusion

inclusion_criteria$criteria enrollments[]$additional_inclusion
scope every enrollment the one enrollment that declares it
path $/inclusion_criteria/criteria[] $/enrollments[]/additional_inclusion[]
types on the criterion has_event has_event, age_range, isoyear_range
types under implementation: no_prior_value, only_prior_value no_prior_value, only_prior_value

A has_event entry generates the same column name in both places. Two entries that generate one column name are one criterion written twice, so tteplan_read_spec() refuses the pair. That holds when both entries are global, and when one is global and one is per-enrollment.

inclusion_criteria$additional_inclusion is refused. That name belongs to an enrollment. In the container, it names a path that swereg does not read.

An isoyear_range entry limits one enrollment to trials registered in a range of ISO years.

additional_inclusion:
  - name: "Trial registration 2008-2016"
    type: isoyear_range
    min: 2008
    max: 2016

tteplan_apply_exclusions() writes the column eligible_isoyears_<min>_<max>, here eligible_isoyears_2008_2016. An age_range in the same enrollment stays in force beside it. tteplan_read_spec() refuses the entry in these cases:

  • min or max is missing, or is not one whole number.
  • min is above max.
  • The range is not inside inclusion_criteria$isoyears.
  • The enrollment already declares an isoyear_range.
  • The entry is in inclusion_criteria$criteria.

The range limits trial registration only, and follow-up continues past max. A 4-week enrollment period that crosses min or max recruits only from its weeks inside the range.

An enrollment takes at most one age_range. Every age_range writes the one column eligible_age, so a second entry would replace the first. tteplan_read_spec() refuses the second entry.

What each rule computes

The schema says which keys a specification may carry. This section says what a rule built from them computes. Its tables come from .TTE_SPEC_RULE_FORMS and .TTE_SPEC_WINDOW_FORMS, in R/tteplan_spec_forms.R. Each worked case below is run when this vignette is built. Its example is read by tteplan_read_spec(), and then compiled by tteplan_apply_exclusions() or tteplan_apply_derived_confounders(). The printed column is the code’s own output. tests/testthat/test-tteplan-spec-forms.R checks the same cases, and it fails when the code accepts a rule type that the registry does not hold.

Every eligibility column is combined with AND into eligible. A person-week enters a trial only when every column is TRUE.

The forms

form type accepted in column written
Calendar years (none) inclusion_criteria$isoyears eligible_isoyears
An event before baseline has_event inclusion_criteria$criteria, enrollments[]$additional_inclusion eligible_has_<variable>_<window>
An age band age_range enrollments[]$additional_inclusion eligible_age, one per enrollment
A calendar range for one enrollment isoyear_range enrollments[]$additional_inclusion eligible_isoyears_<min>_<max>
No earlier week at a value no_prior_value inclusion_criteria$criteria, enrollments[]$additional_inclusion, exclusion_criteria, enrollments[]$additional_exclusion eligible_no_<variable>_<window>
Every observed earlier week at a value only_prior_value inclusion_criteria$criteria, enrollments[]$additional_inclusion, exclusion_criteria, enrollments[]$additional_exclusion eligible_only_<variable>_<window>
No event before baseline (none) exclusion_criteria, enrollments[]$additional_exclusion eligible_no_<variable>_<window>
No event at any time (none) exclusion_criteria, enrollments[]$additional_exclusion eligible_no_<variable>_lifetime_before_and_after_baseline
Any of several columns (none) exclusion_criteria, enrollments[]$additional_exclusion The form’s pattern, with <variable> the joined name
A computed confounder (none) confounders rd_no_<variable>_<window>

Calendar years

  • Source: The skeleton’s isoyear column.
  • Computes: TRUE in a week whose ISO year lies from the first to the second year, both included.
  • Unobserved weeks: A week’s own ISO year decides. No other week is read.

2018-51 FALSE

2019-01 TRUE
2019-02 TRUE
2019-03 TRUE
2019-04 TRUE

An event before baseline

  • Source: A logical column. A list of columns is combined with OR.
  • Computes: TRUE in a week when at least one earlier week inside the window is TRUE. The week itself is never in its own window.
  • Unobserved weeks: A week with no row is not in the window. An NA week follows any(): the result is NA when the window holds an NA week and no TRUE week.

type: has_event

  source_variable: osd_f64
  window: lifetime_before_baseline

2018-50 FALSE FALSE
2018-51 TRUE FALSE
2018-52 FALSE TRUE
2019-01 FALSE TRUE
2019-02 FALSE TRUE
2019-03 FALSE TRUE
2019-04 FALSE TRUE

An age band

  • Source: A numeric column, normally rd_age_continuous.
  • Computes: TRUE in a week whose value is from min to max, both included. The value is compared as stored. On a continuous age, max: 54 excludes an age of 54.5.
  • Unobserved weeks: A week’s own value decides. No other week is read.

No earlier week at a value

  • Source: One column, compared with value. Normally a character column.
  • Computes: TRUE in a week when no earlier week inside the window holds value. The week itself is never in its own window.
  • Unobserved weeks: A week with no row, and an NA week, hold no value, so neither breaks the rule.

Every observed earlier week at a value

  • Source: One column, compared with value. Normally a character column.
  • Computes: TRUE in a week when every earlier week inside the window that holds a value holds value. The week itself is never in its own window.
  • Unobserved weeks: A week with no row, and an NA week, hold no value, so neither breaks the rule. A window with no observed week therefore passes: the rule does not require any week at value.

  value: treated
  window: 2

No event at any time

  • Source: A logical column. It MUST NOT be an outcome variable, because this window reads the weeks after time zero.
  • Computes: FALSE in every week of a person when any of the person’s weeks is TRUE, before or after baseline. It removes the whole person.
  • Unobserved weeks: An NA week is skipped (any(na.rm = TRUE)).

  window: lifetime_before_and_after_baseline

Any of several columns

  • Source: A list of logical columns. swereg ORs them into one column named after all of them, joined by __. The same list works in a has_event rule and in a computed confounder. Do not give a washout a list. tteplan_read_spec() accepts it, and the compiler then stops with a data.table error, because OR does not apply to a character column.
  • Computes: As for the form that holds the list, on the combined column.
  • Unobserved weeks: As for the form that holds the list.

  source_variable: [osd_c, can_c]
  window: lifetime_before_baseline

A computed confounder

  • Source: A logical column. A list of columns is combined with OR.
  • Computes: TRUE in a week when NO earlier week inside the window is TRUE. The name says so: rd_no_. swereg names the column, and a variable key on a computed confounder is replaced. computed: true is what makes it computed. Every rule block accepts the same key, and no rule reads it.
  • Unobserved weeks: A week with no row is not in the window. An NA week follows any(): the result is NA when the window holds an NA week and no TRUE week.
name: "Diabetes in the 2 weeks before baseline"
implementation:
  computed: true
  source_variable: osd_e11
  window: 2
isoyearweek osd_e11 rd_no_osd_e11_2wk
2018-49 FALSE TRUE
2018-50 FALSE TRUE
2018-51 TRUE TRUE
2018-52 FALSE FALSE
2019-01 FALSE FALSE
2019-02 FALSE TRUE
2019-03 FALSE TRUE
2019-04 FALSE TRUE

The windows

A window counts ISO weeks on the calendar, not rows. A week with no row therefore still takes up its place in the window.

written in the column name accepted in meaning
lifetime_before_baseline everbefore every rule with a window, and every computed confounder Every earlier week of the person.
12 12wk every rule with a window, and every computed confounder The 12 ISO weeks before the week, counted on the calendar and not on the rows. A bare number is weeks.
2 years 104wk every rule with a window, and every computed confounder A whole number of years, with year or years. One year is 52 weeks, so the column name gives the weeks.
lifetime_before_and_after_baseline lifetime_before_and_after_baseline exclusion_criteria and additional_exclusion, on a non-washout Every week of the person, after baseline included.
12.5 12wk every rule with a window, with no message A fraction is truncated to whole weeks: 12.5 reads as 12. Write a whole number.
52 weeks refused A unit other than year is refused. Write the bare number 52.
6 months refused Months are refused. Write the weeks as a bare number.
1.5 years refused A fraction of a year is refused. Write the weeks, 78.
  • An inclusion rule MAY leave out window. It then reads lifetime_before_baseline.
  • An exclusion rule and a computed confounder MUST state window. tteplan_read_spec() stops without one.
  • Every window ends at the week before the week it is evaluated in. No window ends earlier, and none starts at the week itself.

What a specification cannot express

  • A count or a duration. No rule counts weeks, so “at least 12 weeks of treatment” has no form. only_prior_value over a window of 12 weeks comes closest, with the limit that its row states. Anything else needs a column built in the skeleton.
  • AND across columns. A list of columns is combined with OR only. Two rules give AND, because every eligibility column is combined with AND.
  • A threshold on a number. Only age_range compares a number, and only against min and max. Any other threshold needs a logical column built in the skeleton.
  • A window that ends before the week before baseline, such as a lag of 4 weeks. Every window ends at the week before.
  • Information after baseline, except the person-level window, which removes the whole person. No inclusion rule reads a week after the week it is evaluated in.
  • A derived treatment variable. treatment$implementation$variable MUST name a skeleton column, and it is read as it stands.
  • A derived outcome, other than a list of outcome columns, which is combined with OR.

A column built in the skeleton is the route for each of these. A rule then reads that column as it reads any other.

The enrollment family

An enrollment MAY set family, a short label that groups enrollments in the results workbook.

enrollments:
  - id: "01"
    name: "Statin initiation vs none"
    family: "Main"
  - id: "02"
    name: "Statin initiation vs none, age 54-60"
    family: "Sens: age 54-60"

The label changes no cohort, model or estimate. $export_tables() shows it in the Family column of the Summary sheet. $reload_spec() applies a new family as a label change, so the cached results stay valid.

tteplan_read_spec() stops, and tteplan_check_spec() reports a row of kind enrollment_family, in two cases:

  • A family is not one non-empty character string. Quote a value that YAML reads as a number, such as family: "2008".
  • Some enrollments set family, and others do not. When one enrollment sets it, every enrollment MUST set it.

The minimum-events exemption

An enrollment MAY set minimum_events_rule_exempt, one logical. With true, the minimum-events rule withholds no estimate of that comparison. An enrollment without the key is not exempt.

A negative-control enrollment normally sets minimum_events_rule_exempt: true. A negative control is read for its estimate, whatever its precision, because the question it answers is whether that estimate sits near the null. Withholding it for too few expected events removes the very check the control exists to give. Set the key on every negative-control enrollment, age subgroups included, and state in the spec why a control that leaves it unset does so.

enrollments:
  - id: "18"
    name: "Statin initiation vs none"
    minimum_events_rule_exempt: true

s3 still computes the rule for each ETT of the enrollment and stores its verdict. The Minimum events and Longest reportable sheets show that verdict, and the comparison name ends with (exempt). $reload_spec() applies a changed value as a cosmetic change, so s1 and s2 output stays valid. $export(), $export_tables() and $print_target_checklist() then stop until $s3_analyze() reruns.

tteplan_read_spec() stops, and tteplan_check_spec() reports a row of kind enrollment_rule_exempt, when the value is not one logical. A number, a string, a null value, NA and a sequence are refused, and the message names the enrollment id.

The feasibility horizon

A spec MAY set the top-level key feasibility_follow_up_weeks, one positive whole number of weeks. It adds a horizon at which s3 computes only the minimum-events rule.

feasibility_follow_up_weeks: 260

The value MAY be longer than every horizon of an enrollment. The ETT grid then gets one more ETT of that length for that enrollment and each outcome. s1 enrolls the enrollment to that horizon. Only the two Minimum events sheets show these ETTs. A value that is not longer than every horizon of an enrollment adds no ETT to it. $reload_spec() treats a change of the key as structural.

tteplan_read_spec() stops, and tteplan_check_spec() reports a row of kind feasibility_follow_up_weeks, when the value is not one positive whole number. A logical, a string, a null value, NA, 0, a negative number, a fraction, an infinite number and a sequence are refused. The message names the key.

A horizon for some comparisons only

A follow_up entry MAY set only_enrollments, a list of enrollment ids. The horizon then applies only to those enrollments. An entry without the key applies to every enrollment.

follow_up:
  - { label: "6 months", weeks: 26 }
  - { label: "1 year",   weeks: 52 }
  - { label: "3 years",  weeks: 156, only_enrollments: [M01] }

The ETT grid holds the 156-week horizon for enrollment M01 and for no other enrollment, and a dropped ETT takes no ETT id. YAML reads only_enrollments: M01 and only_enrollments: [M01] as the same value, so a single id is a list of one. $reload_spec() treats a change of the key as structural.

tteplan_read_spec() stops, and tteplan_check_spec() reports a row of kind follow_up_only_enrollments, in these cases:

  • The list is empty.
  • An element is not a string. Quote an id that YAML reads as a number.
  • The list repeats an id.
  • An id names no enrollment of the spec.

The message names the follow-up label and the bad value.

only_enrollments cannot name the feasibility horizon of feasibility_follow_up_weeks. That horizon is added to an enrollment when it is longer than every horizon of that enrollment.

The 26-week horizon above is not a whole number of years. It takes the minimum-events decision of the 52-week horizon of the same comparison and outcome. Section 1.8.6 of vignette("tte-methods") states that rule.

What you see when a key is refused

tteplan_read_spec() reports every refused key in one message, and reads no data first. Each finding lists the keys its context accepts.

spec_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "spec_v001.yaml")
writeLines(
  c(
    "inclusion_criteria:",
    "  isoyears: [2010, 2023]",
    "  additional_inclusion:",
    "    - name: \"Recorded gender dysphoria diagnosis\"",
    "      type: has_event",
    "      implementation:",
    "        source_variable: osd_f64",
    "        window: lifetime_before_baseline"
  ),
  spec_path
)
msg <- tryCatch(swereg::tteplan_read_spec(spec_path), error = conditionMessage)
cat(sub(tempdir(), "<tempdir>", msg, fixed = TRUE))
#> <tempdir>/spec_v001.yaml carries 1 key swereg does not accept.
#>   $/inclusion_criteria/additional_inclusion
#>     Unknown key 'additional_inclusion'. $/inclusion_criteria accepts: criteria, isoyears.

The report names one key, not six. The walk stops at a refused key, because the schema declares no context below it. Move the entries into criteria, and swereg reads each one.

A misspelt key gets the same message.

writeLines(
  c("inclusion_criteria:", "  isoyear: 2010"),
  spec_path
)
msg <- tryCatch(swereg::tteplan_read_spec(spec_path), error = conditionMessage)
cat(sub(tempdir(), "<tempdir>", msg, fixed = TRUE))
#> <tempdir>/spec_v001.yaml carries 1 key swereg does not accept.
#>   $/inclusion_criteria/isoyear
#>     Unknown key 'isoyear'. $/inclusion_criteria accepts: criteria, isoyears.

Where the gate runs

tteplan_read_spec() calls the gate on the specification as written, before any normalisation. swereg writes derived keys back into the specification as it reads it: window_weeks, source_variable_combined, variable_combined, and the two-field observed_var. The schema names none of them, because the schema describes the input.

R/ holds two calls to yaml::yaml.load(). One is in tteplan_read_spec(). Three functions read a specification through it: tteplan_from_spec_and_registrystudy(), tteplan_excel_spec_summary() and the plan’s own $reload_spec() method. The other call is in tteplan_check_spec(), which returns problems and no specification. No path into a specification skips the gate.

Check a specification without stopping

tteplan_check_spec() reads one specification and returns a data.table with one row per problem. It reports the keys the gate refuses, and it continues past them. It also reports these problems:

  • An enrollment id is missing, or is not one non-empty character string or one number.
  • Two or more enrollments carry the same id.
  • study$implementation$version differs from the spec_vNNN in the file name.

tteplan_read_spec() stops on a missing, bad or repeated id, because $reload_spec() and the Summary sheet find an enrollment by its id. It does not compare the version with the file name. ?tteplan_check_spec lists the eleven problem kinds.

See also

  • vignette("tte-workflow", package = "swereg") for the whole specification, and for the pipeline that reads it.
  • ?tteplan_read_spec for the observation contract and the window conversion rules.
